trust_model.details: The ONLY trust assumption is the genesis/checkpoint block hash (set via owner-only set_genesis_tip). Every subsequent block is verified via PoW (hash < target) + chain linkage (prev == tip) + retarget clamp (at boundaries) + Merkle proof (txid ∈ block) + anchor recomputation (bh matches verified inputs). A malicious relayer cannot insert a fake block, an orphan block, or a fabricated anchor.
trust_model.remaining_trust: genesis block hash + the code itself (Cairo contract + test scripts)

not_done_open.description: The contract enforces the retarget clamp at 2016-block boundaries but does not fully implement Bitcoin Core's GetNextWorkRequired for testnet (min-difficulty rule when gap > 20 min). Between boundaries, the PoW check is the security floor. On mainnet, the between-boundary bits==prev_bits assert would be added.
not_done_open.impact: A malicious relayer could submit a testnet block with non-standard bits (e.g., very easy difficulty) between boundaries, as long as the hash satisfies that easy target. The PoW check prevents forged blocks (the hash must be < target(bits)), but the difficulty could be lower than the network's actual difficulty. On mainnet, this is closed by asserting bits == prev_bits between boundaries.

not_done_open.description: The contract is append-only — it tracks a single chain_tip and does not support reorgs. If the Bitcoin network reorgs, the contract's tip may point to an orphaned block. Anchors on the orphaned branch would still pass verify_anchor (they're valid blocks), but they may no longer be on the main chain.
not_done_open.impact: In a reorg, anchors on the orphaned branch remain verifiable but are no longer backed by the main chain. The depth gate (6+ confirmations) mitigates this for shallow reorgs. Full reorg handling (cumulative-work-based tip switching) is not implemented.

not_done_open.description: The escrow release enforces coherence >= min_coherence (550000) on-chain. However, the coherence value is supplied by the authorized caller (relayer), not by a multi-party oracle quorum. A malicious relayer could supply a high coherence value (920000) to release the escrow, as long as they're authorized.
not_done_open.impact: The release is gated by the coherence floor, but the coherence value is not independently verified by an oracle quorum. Closing this requires a multi-sig or oracle-based coherence submission mechanism.
